manuscript.Abstract: In a single-centre cohort, 120 adults with chronic fatigue were followed for 18 months. A structured exercise programme reduced symptom scores by 32% compared with usual care.
manuscript.Introduction: Chronic fatigue is common in primary care. Exercise is widely recommended for fatigue management [3]. We aimed to test whether a structured exercise programme reduces symptom scores in adults with chronic fatigue.
manuscript.Methods: We enrolled 120 adults in a prospective cohort; every participant received the structured exercise programme. Symptom scores were measured at baseline and at 12 months. Baseline and follow-up scores were compared with a t test.
manuscript.Results: Mean symptom scores fell by 32% from baseline (p = 0.01). No participant withdrew.
manuscript.Discussion: This proves that structured exercise works.
manuscript.Conclusion: Structured exercise reduces symptom scores in adults with chronic fatigue.

references.title: Exercise therapy in chronic fatigue: a cohort study
Measuring fatigue severity in primary care
